title: Paperclip: Open Source Human Control Plane for AI Labor — Dotta Bippa
talk_summary: Most value is in the workflow-gate and per-agent-instruction practices, not the product marketing.

takeaways.what_they_do: Configure workflows so when an assignee finishes a task, a QA agent must boot and review it, and a separate manager/approver signs off; coder and reviewer iterate between the two roles.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when the assignee is complete uh is finished with this task, you must have the QA agent boot and give a review on it

takeaways.what_they_do: Maintains a living instruction block per agent, appending rules whenever the agent misbehaves (e.g. always give a best-guess fix, don't write the whole test suite).
takeaways.evidence_quote: if there's a blocker, tell us your best guess on how to fix it. Don't just say it's blocked

takeaways.technique: Per-agent and per-project budgets, cheap models for low-intelligence roles
takeaways.what_they_do: Tracks monthly spend, sets budgets per agent/project, and routes only the highest-intelligence agents to frontier models while cheaper/free models handle the rest.
takeaways.evidence_quote: everything that you do might not need to pay frontier model prices... Maybe just your most intelligent agents need to do that

takeaways.what_they_do: Stores recurring tasks (PR handling, daily merged-PR Discord digest, changelog) as routines runnable on schedule or manually with variables like branch name, instead of copy-pasting prompts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of kind of having a prompt folder or having to copy and paste um you can create these routines

takeaways.technique: Meta 'skill consultant' agent to diagnose skill usage
takeaways.what_they_do: A dedicated agent inspects other agents' behavior and iterates on whether they are actually using their installed skills correctly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The skill consultant's job is to actually work with the other agents within the organization to make sure that they're using their skills

takeaways.what_they_do: Advises against importing large prebuilt org templates; build each agent, verify quality, and only fan out when justified.
takeaways.evidence_quote: just start with the agents that you need... if you don't take the time to kind of craft for the agents how you expect them to behave, then you won't get good results
